- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after a recent spike (e.g., >70) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model overestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral — adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct — add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment to counteract.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) → model lags by 1–2 days; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to align with sentiment momentum.
